title: Joe Duffy Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Joe Duffy review, checked 7 Nov 2026: OffshoreInsiders prices from $21 a day to $1,249 a year, no refunds, and what outside leaderboards show of his record.
dek: Joe Duffy has sold picks since 1988 and runs OffshoreInsiders.com, where packages cost $21 for a day to $1,249 for a year with no refunds. The site claims "the most units won of all time" but posts no record. A pick marketplace leaderboard showed him near break even in 2026.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record for Joe Duffy. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

glance: OffshoreInsiders.com, 9925 Haynes Bridge Road, Suite #200-186, Alpharetta, GA (contact page). Email only, no phone

short_answer: Joe Duffy runs a real, long running pick business. OffshoreInsiders.com lists a mailing address in Alpharetta, Georgia, an email address, published prices for every package and the date each one runs to. Payment goes through PayPal. In that narrow sense it is legitimate.

Whether his picks make money is not shown on his own site. It claims he has "the most units won of all time" and that over any long period he will hit "near or above the 60 percentile," but it publishes no record, and its FAQ says it is not wise to advertise losing days. Two outside pick marketplaces that sell his picks showed small gains: one at 686-638 with a 0.6% return for 2026, one at 81-69-3 over a period it did not state.

Treat Duffy as an experienced seller whose marketing claims go far beyond the numbers we could find. If you buy, start with a day or a week, record every pick with the line you got, and judge it after a few hundred picks.
pricing_intro: Prices below were shown on the OffshoreInsiders.com package page on 7 Nov 2026. Each package listed the date it would run to if bought that day. Purchases go through PayPal, which also takes cards.
guarantee: OffshoreInsiders does not sell a guarantee. Its FAQ answers "Why not guarantee your picks like some other sites?" at length, says "Anyone who wants a guarantee frankly should not be gambling," and states: "we do not give refunds for occasional losing days." Packages run on consecutive days, like a newspaper subscription, with exceptions only for some monthly or longer buyers.

There is a twist. An OffshoreInsiders page announcing its sister site, PicksDepot.com, says PicksDepot sells Duffy's picks in "Guaranteed Packages" while OffshoreInsiders offers "lower-priced, non-guaranteed packages." We did not read the PicksDepot guarantee terms, so we cannot say whether that means cash, credit or more picks.

claims_note: The biggest claims come with no numbers at all. "The most units won of all time" names no total, no period and no source, and nothing on the site lets a reader check it.

The FAQ is unusually frank about how it markets. Asked why the site never talks about losers, it says the best products do not advertise bad reviews and that "it would not be wise to advertise losing days," while promising "There will be no inaccurate records posted." In other words, what you see is chosen to sell. Asked where records are documented, it calls that a "simple question, not a simple answer" and points to an article without giving a record.

The bios disagree with each other. One says he has had a winning March Madness every year since 1998, another says since 1988. The FAQ also carries a badge reading "Verified by CapperTek on 10-8-2020"; CapperTek's own page lists OffshoreInsiders as a verified service, but its documented record did not load for our check.
record: What a buyer can check outside OffshoreInsiders: PicksDepot, the sister site announced by OffshoreInsiders, showed a leaderboard on 7 Nov 2026 whose top rows matched the SportsCapping current season board exactly. It ranked Joe Duffy 22nd with 686-638, 51.8% wins, average odds of -106, a 0.6% return and $923 profit. SportsCapping says its board counts all picks since 1 Jan on flat $100 bets. At -106 a bettor needs about 51.5% to break even, so this is close to flat. StatsAlt, another marketplace, showed him at 81-69-3, +26.33 units and +$2,633 profit, without saying what period that covers. All of these sites sell his picks, and we could not open the full pick logs behind the numbers, so they are third party figures, not audits.

What is the seller's own marketing: every claim on OffshoreInsiders.com, from "most units won of all time" to the 60% target. The site has no results page we could find, and its FAQ says it is not set up to post plays after they start, though it says it may add that.
We found no court or regulator action involving Joe Duffy or OffshoreInsiders in our searches.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition Joe Duffy is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how his picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: the OffshoreInsiders FAQ says he will hit near or above 60% over time. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: We found no customer reviews of Joe Duffy or OffshoreInsiders on any review site we checked, and the forum mentions we could open are short and say nothing about results. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: CapperTek's review page for OffshoreInsiders said there were no reviews, SmartCustomer (formerly SiteJabber) showed 0 reviews, Trustpilot had no page for offshoreinsiders.com, and a Better Business Bureau search returned no matching business. We found no Reddit thread about the service.
On TheRX forum, a member asked whether anyone had used Joe Duffy and OffshoreInsiders and how the picks were. The replies we read on that page did not answer him.

In a TheRX service plays thread, a member posted the day's Joe Duffy Wise Guy and major plays and wrote that they were "Paid and confirmed by me," which shows he bought them. He did not report how they did.

conflicts: The OffshoreInsiders homepage carries a banner link that redirects to an affiliate address at MyBookie, an offshore sportsbook, with the promo code MB50. The site's article list also includes reviews of MyBookie, BetOnline and Bovada. Affiliate deals like these usually pay the referrer when readers sign up or lose. Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators, so check the law where you live.
PicksDepot, which displays the leaderboard quoted above, is OffshoreInsiders' own sister site, and StatsAlt and SportsCapping sell picks too. None of them is a neutral auditor.
strengths: Every package price is published, with the exact date each package runs to.
A mailing address and email are listed, and payment goes through PayPal rather than straight to a bank.
The FAQ is blunt that there is no guarantee and no refund, so a buyer knows the terms before paying.
His picks are listed on outside marketplaces that grade them, which is more than many sellers allow.
concerns: No record on his own site, and an FAQ that says losing days are not advertised.
"Most units won of all time" and the 60% target have no figures behind them; the outside numbers we found were near break even.
No refunds, and no phone support.
The homepage carries an offshore sportsbook affiliate link with a promo code.
Bios on different sites give different start years for the same March Madness claim.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: OffshoreInsiders is a real, long running business with a mailing address, published prices and PayPal checkout. We could not verify his big claims, such as the most units won of all time, because his site publishes no record.
How much does Joe Duffy cost?
On 7 Nov 2026 OffshoreInsiders charged $21 for one day, $129 for a week, $299 for a month, $899 for 100 days and $1,249 for a year, with no refunds for losing days.
Does Joe Duffy have a verified record?

Not a full one. Outside pick marketplaces that sell his picks showed 686-638 with a 0.6% return for 2026 and 81-69-3 over an unstated period, but we could not open the logs behind them, and Watchdog has no graded record for him.

For $21 a day you get every pick he releases, usually 3 to 6 plays according to the FAQ, from a handicapper active since 1988. What is unproven is the 60% the site promises: the outside numbers we found were close to break even, and losing days are not refunded.
